Vocabulary that has nothing to do with the product at all is handled

includeNote: `include` is the surface a stranger reads: everything in the npm tarball,
plus the repository files a stranger lands on from the README. It is not the
same set as `git ls-files`. benchmark/ and packages/core/dev/ are outside it
because they are measurement and diagnostic code rather than product surface,
and the vocabulary rules below are written for product prose. They are still
read end to end by the publication-boundary check, which has no exemptions.
If a file is added to the `files` array in packages/core/package.json, add a
glob for it here in the same commit -- the two lists are the same list seen
from two directions, and check-publication-boundary.mjs fails if they drift.

terms.reason: Framing from a comparison exercise rather than a fact about the software. Factual comparisons stay; the framing goes. The directory `benchmark/` is published on purpose, so a line whose every occurrence of the word is the literal path `benchmark/` is a file reference and is allowed. 'the benchmark', 'our benchmark' and 'a benchmark' are not.
The comparison implementations built alongside this library. Name the actual technology instead ('a hand-rolled S3 integration').

Ambiguous on its own. In this product an auditor is someone reading the audit log, so spell it 'compliance auditor' and the sentence cannot be read any other way. 'auditor' as an example user id in a string literal is fine.
